problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(x-1)^{3n}}{{n}^{n}}=(x-1)^{3}+\frac{(x-1)^{6}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{(x-1)^{9}}{{3}^{3}}+⋯\,.
$$
worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{(x-1)^{3n}}{{n}^{n}}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(x-1)^{3(n+1)}}{(n+1)^{n+1}}\cdot \frac{{n}^{n}}{(x-1)^{3n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(x-1)^{3}}{(n+1)}\cdot {(\frac{n}{n+1})}^{n}| \\  & =|x-1{|}^{3}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{(n+1)}\cdot {(\frac{n}{n+1})}^{n} \\  & =|x-1{|}^{3}\cdot 0\cdot {e}^{-1} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for all $-\infty <x<\infty .$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\infty .$
